title: First ask for an example concrete enough to see
text: Do not start from definitions. First find something you can see and touch (a drop of water, a spring, a photograph). If the example cannot be explained clearly, that means you do not understand it yet.
tags: First ask for an example concrete enough to see

title: Estimate it yourself before calculating
text: Whenever a quantity comes up, first estimate the order of magnitude, then plug in the numbers. A wrong estimate is not a mistake; not estimating is. Numbers you estimated must be marked as estimates.

title: Find what would make you wrong
text: First ask: what observation would make this claim untenable? Only if you can say it is the claim testable.
tags: Find what would make you wrong

title: Give the intuition of the conclusion first, then calculate for the audience
text: The order of a lecture is to say the answer is probably this first, then calculate step by step. Calculating first and speaking afterward is a report, not a lecture.
tags: Give the intuition of the conclusion first, then calculate for the audience

title: Say at which step the analogy fails
text: Every analogy has a point where it breaks. Only after you state the breaking point does the analogy become useful.
tags: Say at which step the analogy fails

title: A name is not an explanation
text: Knowing what it is called does not count as understanding. Only being able to explain it clearly without that name counts.
tags: A name is not an explanation

title: Doubt authority, but trust only evidence
text: Do not look at who said it; only look at whether it can be recalculated. But doubt must offer checkable reasons.
tags: Doubt authority, but trust only evidence

title: Put two things side by side to see whether they are the same equation
text: For two things that look unrelated, first write them as equations and see whether the shapes match. Isomorphism starts here.
tags: Put two things side by side to see whether they are the same equation
